analysis.title: DeskTalk - Not out of the macro woods after NVDA
key_insights: The 'Trump put' was triggered and boosted the AI trade, but risk appetite is already fading and some markets fully reversed the prior day's move.
Recent volatility was not only about one company's leadership. FOMC, dollar strength and AI concerns remain unresolved.
OIS prices over 25bp for Dec despite FOMC pricing easing on the equity correction. Inflation is elevated and the reaction function is more hawkish, so the US front end sees limited relief.
Williams said he would be open to back to back rate hikes 'if that was what was needed'.
Intermediate curve duration has been well bid per the Citi sales desk.
Core PCE on Wednesday is the main event of the holiday shortened week (Citi forecasts 0.27% MoM), with payrolls next Friday as further event risk.
USD strength is largely intact, even while US equities were correcting lower. EURUSD saw 'relentless selling' in a flow driven move per the trader.
USDJPY saw Tokyo supply overnight but 160 remains the line in the sand. The options desk prefers crossJPY over USDJPY for risk expression.
USD strength resumed against EM FX, with ZAR and MXN giving back prior gains, and gold spot struggling to hold gains.

AI concerns persist, shown by copper retracing the prior day's move. The new Congress in January is seen as less data center friendly, and the 'sell the news' reaction to ANT's IPO signals valuation caution.
Few obvious catalysts for a Santa rally per colleague Varshi.
Geopolitics is off the radar. Iran strikes are indicated as more likely in the new year, indirect talks continue, and Brent has fallen below $90, but a settlement may prove elusive.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Main event of the holiday shortened week, a hot print would support the hawkish front end pricing.
Market pricing a hike-leaning path despite the equity correction, limiting front end relief.
Fell as geopolitical risk is seen capped for now.
